correctness.rationale: For H=Z×N and Q=N² with Dirichlet diagonal 4, normalized sine/Fourier point-mass weights are N_H=1-cos(2jk2) and N_Q=(1-cos(2ak1))(1-cos(2bk2)), over omega=4-2cos k1-2cos k2. Their rank-one diagonal resolvent F(ε) is continuous, strictly decreasing, finite at zero, and tends to zero, so Birman–Schwinger gives exactly one simple negative eigenvalue iff lambda>1/F(0). For a critical zero vector, Fourier amplitude is δhat/omega and its norm squared is integral N/omega². Near zero, N_H~2j²k2² yields logarithmic divergence (no ℓ² zero mode), while N_Q~4a²b²k1²k2² yields integrability (one-dimensional ℓ² eigenspace). Polar integration for fixed j gives F_H(0)-F_H(ε)=j²ε log(1/ε)/(4π)+O_j(ε). Dominated convergence gives F_Q(0)-F_Q(ε)=εB_ab+o(ε). Since F(0)-F(ε)=F(0)²(λ-λc)+o(λ-λc), the two claimed coefficients follow. Fourier normalization, multiplicity, positivity, and boundary j,a,b>=1 were checked explicitly. Independent Gauss-Legendre and one-dimensional Green-integral calculations confirm F_H,1=0.3633802276324186; F_Q,1,1=0.30234727368645, B_1,1~0.13661977237 and corner slope~0.669111596, and edge log ratios approach j²/(4π).

final_claim: For the four-diagonal Dirichlet nearest-neighbor Laplacian on Z×N or N² perturbed by one attractive delta at fixed site, the unique negative simple eigenvalue exists iff λ>λc=1/F(0). At λc the half-plane canonical zero-energy solution is non-ℓ² and there is no zero eigenfunction; the quadrant has a one-dimensional ℓ² zero eigenspace. With ε=-E>0 and λ↓λc from above, ε log(1/ε)~[4πF_H,j(0)²/j²](λ-λc) in the half-plane and ε~[F_Q,a,b(0)²/B_a,b](λ-λc) in the quadrant. All at each fixed positive-integer site. The Green formulas, existence thresholds and the j=1 critical value are prior results, not original parts of the theorem.
